description: Same-binary 3080 host-expert placement A/B on the experimental staged P2P integration; not production or long-context qualification.
method: The same candidate server executable and private configuration were used for control and candidate; only Q36_P2P_HOST_EXPERT_BYTES on card 1 changed. Each arm had one cold 64-token warmup, three cold 524-token prompts, three cold 4274-token prompts and three deterministic 128-token decode samples. Server job-start-to-first-token timing includes first-token generation; client timing includes the complete reply. Server and client token counts, cold reuse, successful responses, correct arithmetic answers, decode output hashes and finish reasons were checked.

short.timing_note: Server timing runs from job start to first emitted batch and includes first-token generation; client timing runs to the complete reply.

long.timing_note: Server timing runs from job start to first emitted batch and includes first-token generation; client timing runs to the complete reply.

refused_tighter_placement.calculation: The refused request selected two fewer 75,497,472-byte slices than the baseline on the 3060. Assuming a single-slice change shifts the admission total by that exact slice size, a one-slice reduction would still exceed the reported available memory by 29,519,360 bytes; that intermediate setting was not tested.

limitations: One control-then-candidate order, three samples per arm; thermal and ordering effects were not crossed over, and the measured change is small.
The exact measured code is the parent integration commit; this evidence-only MR adds documentation and does not alter the tested binary.
The model was configured for 262144 context but the longest prompt was 4274 tokens. No 128k/256k recall or coding quality qualification was performed.
The guard sampled VRAM and activity; sampled floors cannot exclude an unsampled transient. The user-confirmed router-poll exception cannot prove no hidden user request.
This experiment does not enable or deploy the setting by default; free memory, model, device order, and workload affect whether it fits.
